## Challenge-phase corrections

The verdicts above are the JUDGES' output. Every `theirs` verdict was then given to a skeptic,
and four came back amended. **Read these before acting on any C-row** — one concession was
withdrawn outright and one finding was reversed in our favour.

**AA-mode change at runtime: PR570 a86cc0f8 "Fix MSAA crash o…** — affects C13, C14, C15

> RESTATED GAP (this is the actionable sentence): both sides fix the same stamp, but theirs fixes it only for third-party shader packs — with one framebuffer, zero `frameBufferTextures`, and no C++ borrow API in their tree, `pair.first == "main"` is provably a no-op for every asset they ship — while ours fixes it for a path that is live in stock play (GPU lightmap and backdrop caches borrow FBO textures from C++ at StarGpuLightmapPass.cpp:139/274/281/285 and StarBackdropPass.cpp:76-77), proves it on hardware with an internal control, and additionally closes the orphaned-sampler half that their patch leaves open at tree/source/application/StarRenderer_opengl.cpp:641-646. TWO AMENDMENTS TO THE VERDICT AS WRITTEN. (1) simplicity: theirs -> TIE. Withdraw the concession. Its premise, "`== \"main\"` cannot be re-broken from asset data", is false: an effect that samples "main" (the natural post-process) silently gets a multisample texture under their rule with no opt-out, whereas our undeclared-is-single-sample default fails safe. Their remaining edge is only "one site, no cross-artifact agreement", which the verdict already offsets against the 343-line commit the line is buried in. (2) coverage: strike "the identity early-out at :1340 then matches the corpse". Their m_currentFrameBuffer is a RefPtr and the early-out is pointer identity, so the corpse it holds alive can never be matche…

**Proving the cellular lighting correct and fast** — affects C16, C17, C18

> Two corrections, neither of which flips the verdict. (1) THE LEAD QUALITY FINDING IS REASONED WRONGLY. "Production IS the oracle... an attenuation-math regression moves both and the tests still pass" is false. pointLightingReference (source/base/StarCellularLightArray.cpp:379-464) and spreadJacobiReference (:468) are independent reimplementations — separate attenuation arithmetic, a separate obstacleLineAttenuation over a flat obstacle list, and a deliberately different spread algorithm (Jacobi vs production's Gauss-Seidel). Only the PARAMETERS are shared, not the math; a production math regression turns these tests red. Ours is a differential two-implementation oracle, a stronger construct than credited. The finding survives in restated, weaker form: a differential oracle written FROM production pins DRIFT, not TRUTH — it cannot detect a bug that was already present at authoring time, and we have no absolute anchor on the attenuation model the way theirs does at cellular_lighting_test.cpp:50-52. (2) THE BIGGEST FACT WAS MISSED, AND IT REORDERS THE PROPOSALS. Our 20 lighting tests execute in ZERO CI jobs; theirs execute in five. Theirs label core_tests NoAssets (their CMakeLists:94-95), their base testPreset filters on that label (CMakePresets.json:221), and build.yml runs ctest through those presets on five platforms. Ours are all in game_tests, which our own CMakeLists:495 p…

**Recomputing only the changed part of the lightmap** — affects —

> Three amendments, none of which flip an axis. 1. STRENGTHEN the performance axis; the filed caveat against us is miscast. At StarWorldClient.cpp:2401 our shipped default takes `skipCpuCalc = lightingGpu && !shadowCompare && m_gpuLightingActive`, which skips `m_lightingCalculator.calculate()` outright (counted by lighting.cpu.calc.skipped/.ran at :2395-2398). Their entire patch optimises the CPU CellularLightArray propagation — a stage our default configuration does not execute. The verdict's caveat ("our own #128 GPU matrix puts the propagation they target at lightPoint ~1750µs + spread ~812µs, i.e. the bigger prize is the one we archived") conflates two different stages: those are GPU-pass timings, and their CPU-array scroll does not touch them. The correct statement is: the bigger prize is real and it lives on the GPU; their code does not address it; what transfers is the IDEA (scroll-trigger + separate point channels), not the patch. That makes PROPOSED item (4) the load-bearing one and item (4)'s "meter first" gate the right call. 2. TIGHTEN the second defeat's provenance and magnitude. The verdict attributes the window-size breathing to our #127 measurement ("±2 tiles"). It is now confirmable directly from THEIR tree and is structural, not empirical: worldTileRect() takes ceil(screenTilesF + frac(camera min)), which flips the size by ±1 per axis whenever the fractional ca…

**point lights: cost versus fidelity** — affects C10, C11, C12

> The verdict stands as "mixed", and the axis given to them (simplicity) survives — if anything it was understated: the sites that must change together to change the point-light model are 2 (their pointLightFlood + lineAttenuation, one file) versus 8 for us across four files and two languages (StarCellularLightArray.cpp:8, :81, :170, :310, :379; StarCellularLightArray.hpp:541; lightingPoint.frag:34, :86). ONE load-bearing sub-claim must be struck and reversed. The verdict's quality axis reads "Verification: we have a live in-game oracle ... with a 5-min 0-mismatch soak; they have none." That is wrong in our favour. lightingGpuShadowCompare is default-OFF (StarRootLoader.cpp:148); our own shader-pass comment calls it "permanently red for a known unrelated reason -- it can detect a change but cannot certify identity" (StarGpuLightmapPass.cpp:151-152); and board.md:734 (#106) records that it was "structurally unable to ULP-gate (promote0=empty point pass; promote0.5=CDL gap swamps)" — i.e. it cannot certify the point path at promote 0.5, which is the shipping default. The 5-minute 0-mismatch soak at board.md:724 is the DIRTY-GATE validate shadow from the #105 spike, which board.md:744 records as staked and archived on feat/dirty-region; it is not evidence for shadowCompareFull.
